hero.title: Spread of Buddhism & Royal Patronage
hero.description: An analytical study of how Buddhism evolved from a local sect in Magadha to a world religion through state support and missionary zeal.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Key historical markers from the birth of Buddha to the institutionalization of Buddhism.

cards.details: Life of Siddhartha Gautama; emergence of Buddhism as a reaction against Vedic orthodoxy.
Ashoka's Kalinga War and his subsequent conversion to Buddhism, leading to state-sponsored missionary expansion.
Fourth Buddhist Council under Kanishka in Kashmir, marking the formal split into Hinayana and Mahayana.

items.title: A.K.A.S.K
items.decryption: Remember the primary royal patrons of the four major Buddhist councils.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assuming all Buddhist rulers were monks; many patronized Buddhism while maintaining state administrative duties.
Confusing the Second Council (Vaisali) with the Third (Pataliputra) regarding the sectarian schism.
Believing Buddhism disappeared entirely from India after the Gupta period.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Magadha: The Heartland
  • North-West: Silk Road Connectivity
  • Sri Lanka: Third Council Influence

Personalities

  • Ashoka: The Great Evangelist
  • Kanishka: Patron of Mahayana
  • Harshavardhana: The Last Great Patron
  • Mechanisms of Spread:
    • State Patronage: Grants for Monasteries (Viharas).
    • Missionary Diplomacy: Ashoka sending his children (Mahendra and Sanghamitra) to Sri Lanka.
    • Monastic Networks: Sangh architecture becoming the backbone of Buddhist economy.
